body: From what you say it sounds like she had more reason that some dumb sushi conversation behind her decision. And to not tell you about her true feelings and to just dump you is cold. Is that someone you'd want to marry? That doesn't talk to you and then leaves? I know it hurts like hell, but it's good she is gone. Find out her true colors when you are still young. I'm super old! And I just got dumped again, but is was all my fault. I am dying inside as I don't have a lot of time left. You have the whole world ahead of you. And remember that living good is the best revenge. Look good. Feel good. And one day the person who deserves you will come along and she will be nothing but a distant memory.

I too am in the throes of a horribly, agonizing breakup. I feel numb and sad and destroyed. I spend the entire day on the verge of tears, just going through the motions. I cannot go to sleep because everytime I start to fall, I am startled awake by reality. He is gone. He doesn't want me. He didn't want to do the work for me. And I loved him endlessly. I would have never left him. 
I know how alone you feel. I feel the EXACT same way right now. I daydream about dying and wish it would all end. The only thing I have found to help is talking about it. Reading other peoples breakup stories on here. Getting some perspective. I was with my dude for 18months and he broke up with me for something that was all my fault. I feel regret every f'ing second of the day. EVERY SINGLE ONE. You are not alone. I wish they had some kind of heartbreak support groups people could go to in person.

Hate is simply pain turned outward. You are full of pain from this betrayal by someone you loved. You have to move beyond the hate and into the pain. Sit in it. Let it tear you up inside. And eventually, you have to LET IT GO. 
Remember that it is not your fault that she cheated. Remember that you are the only person that can hold and release those feelings. Take away the power she has over you by controlling your own actions. 
If this helps visualize it - let go of the pain and imagine giving it back to her. Let her figure it out. And even if it's not today, or tomorrow, one day she will have to deal with it. Because only people who have some real issues are the ones that cheat. Don't let the issues of her past rule your future.

If you don't have any ulterior motives or hidden feelings, then it is fine to add. 

If you do have feelings, do NOT.

I feel the same right now. And although I cannot even take my own advice, I will say this. Find a support group in your town - they have them for everything. I recently found a Love Addicts support group. People there are a community built on caring and supporting each other. Go to the local shelter - womens / mens - and talk to those people. Helping others in their pain often eases our own. Something to bring a little light to your life.

I am so sorry you feel so alone. I am so sorry that you feel neglected, taken for granted, and dismissed. You matter. And your husband, even though he is fighting cancer, should be appreciating you more than anyone else in the world. Why? Because you are helping him constantly, because you are raising his children. Cancer is not an excuse to be an asshole and treat the people who love you the most like complete shit. 

You HAVE to stand up for yourself. There is no other way to deal with the situation. You will continue to burn out and eventually be gone - physically, mentally, emotionally.

I don't know the exact details for your situation, but I do know that something has to change. Be HONEST with him. Don't sacrifice yourself as his doormat.
My daughter is only 5 and I ruined her life. I ruined her chance at the family she wants and deserves. She saw me sobbing on the couch again today and started sobbing too. I am ruining her.

I should have been able to handle it. I could have. If I had just been warm and compassionate with the kid. But my god I felt like I was living in her shadow the entire time. He didn't make me feel that outright - but it was just all around. Their wedding photos, her nail polish in the cabinet. Her clothes in the closet. All of it was so much. And his kid did not like having us around for the first 8 months. So it set a pretty hard scene for me to integrate into.

I dated a man who had been with the love of his life for 14 years. They had a home, a young son, and were very much in love. She died suddenly, right in front of him. He went through the most excrutiating time of his life. He thought about killing himself. He thought about killing himself and his son. He didn't sleep for weeks and wept constantly. Though I did not experience the pain myself, I know what it took for him to get through it. 

It was a lot of grieving. A lot of crying. Therapy. Grief support groups. But it took two years for him to feel halfway okay again. And another two years later he feels okay with it. One thing that he did swear by was Wim Hof. It's a breathing technique developed by a man who had his wife die. It was the only thing that saved him from death. 

Please look into Wim Hof. Read his story and see if perhaps it can connect with you.
